title: Jobs
objective: Say your job with I'm a… / I'm an… and ask What do you do?
intro_md:
[L1: In this lesson you learn ten job words. You say your job with "I'm a…" or "I'm an…" (an before a vowel sound: an engineer, an artist). You also learn the question "What do you do?" — learn it as one piece; the grammar comes later. In English-speaking countries this question is normal, friendly small talk — it is not rude.]
{{l1_contrast:article_a_an_jobs}}
notes: TODO_audio: exercises 2 and 6 need recorded audio; the quoted text in the prompt stands in for the recording. Flashcards (exercise 1) need audio fronts per the L05 exemplar.

new_vocabulary.example_sentence: What do you do? — I'm a cook.

exercises.prompt: job · What do you do? · doctor · nurse · cook · driver · waiter · engineer · artist · police officer
exercises.rationale: Establish form-meaning link for the ten job items with audio before any production; FSRS flips direction on second exposure.

exercises.prompt: [audio, 0.75x] 'She's a doctor.' — [L1: What is her job?]
exercises.rationale: Word-level comprehension of the job after 'a'; distractors force listening to the word, not guessing from topic.

options.label: doctor
options.rationale: Heard after 'a' — the job slot in the I'm-a frame.

options.label: nurse
options.rationale: Same medical association; catches topic-guessing instead of word-level listening.

options.label: waiter
options.rationale: Ends in the same unstressed -er; catches suffix-only listening.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Match the job to the sentence. Look at the small word before the job.]
exercises.rationale: Receptive noticing of a vs an sorted by first sound (vowel-initial engineer/artist vs consonant-initial cook/nurse) before the rule is produced.

exercises.prompt: A: What do you do?  B: I'm ___ engineer.
exercises.rationale: First forced a/an choice before a vowel sound; 'the' catches overgeneralized definite article from L1s with one default article.
Minimal contrast pair in one item: the same learner must switch a → an on sound, not memorize per word.

exercises.prompt: [audio, 0.75x] 'I'm a doctor.' — [L1: What do you hear?]
exercises.rationale: The article is a weak /ə/ and nearly inaudible; perceiving it targets article drop, the top predicted transfer error (es 'Soy médico', zh/ar no article).

options.label: I'm a doctor.
options.rationale: The small word 'a' is there — English always needs it before a job.

options.label: I'm doctor.
options.rationale: Missing 'a'. Direct transfer from article-less frames (es 'Soy médico'); English requires the article.

exercises.rationale: The chunk contains 'do' twice, which confuses beginners; ordering forces noticing the fixed question shape. Predicted in-situ error: 'You do what?' (zh/vi transfer).

exercises.prompt: A: What ___ you do?  B: I'm ___ waiter.
exercises.rationale: 'are' catches the predicted blend with six lessons of be-questions ('What are you do?'); second blank re-tests the article under dialogue load.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Match the question to the answer.]
exercises.rationale: All three personal-info questions the learner must field in L17/L18; discriminating them matters because every answer starts with I'm. Recycles L03 and L05 (N-2 rule).

exercises.prompt: [L1: Talk with the AI: say hello, give your name, say your job. Then ask the AI: What do you do?]
exercises.rationale: Integrates L01+L03 chunks with today's job frame in real time; the learner also asks the question (initiative), rehearsing the L17 dialogue role. Counts toward guided-interaction minutes.
